questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly lists the set of letters in the word "BANANA" using proper set notation?

options.why: Includes repeated elements instead of listing each distinct letter once.
Omits the vowel $A$ from the set of letters.
Uses parentheses for an ordered tuple instead of curly braces for a set.

questions.solution_text:
A set contains distinct elements without repetition.
$\{B, A, N\}$

questions.question_text: Let $P$ be the set of two-digit prime numbers less than $20$. What is the value of $|P|$?

options.why: Counts all prime numbers less than $20$ including single-digit primes $2, 3, 5, 7$.
Incorrectly includes the composite number $15$ or odd non-prime as a prime.
Misses one of the two-digit primes in the range $11, 13, 17, 19$.

questions.question_text: Let $S = \{1, 3, 5, 7\}$. Which of the following sets is a subset of $S$?

options.why: The element $4$ does not belong to set $S$.
The element $9$ does not belong to set $S$.
The element $0$ does not belong to set $S$.

questions.solution_text:
Every element of $\{1, 5\}$ is in $S = \{1, 3, 5, 7\}$.
$\{1, 5\} \subseteq S$

questions.question_text: If $A = \{10, 20, 30\}$ and $B = \{20, 40, 60\}$, which set represents $A \cup B$?

options.why: Finds the intersection $A \cap B$ instead of the union $A \cup B$.
Lists the shared element $20$ twice instead of once.
Omits the common element $20$ entirely from the union.
Finds the union $A \cup B$ instead of the intersection $A \cap B$.
Claims there is no common element when $15$ is in both sets.
Includes $5$ which is only in set $B$ and not in set $A$.

questions.question_text: Given universal set $\xi = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}$ and $A = \{1, 4, 9\}$, what is $A'$?

options.why: Returns set $A$ itself instead of its complement $A'$.
Lists only the prime numbers in $\xi$ rather than all non-elements of $A$.
Incorrectly keeps $4$ in the complement even though $4 \in A$.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of sets are disjoint (mutually exclusive)?

options.why: They share the element $2$, so their intersection is not empty.
They share common multiples such as $15, 30, 45$.
They share common factors $1, 2, 3, 6$.

questions.solution_text:
All prime numbers are positive integers ($2, 3, 5, \dots$), so $A \cap B = \varnothing$.
$A = \{\text{prime numbers}\}, B = \{\text{negative integers}\}$

options.why: Calculates $n(A \cup B)$ instead of the cardinality of its complement.
Counts only even non-members and misses one element in the complement.
Calculates $n(A')$ instead of $n((A \cup B)')$.
